add_a_ring: Merge the ring branch into the packaging branch with --no-ff; resolve only packaging-side conflicts (showcase/bestiarium/collection.json, README, registration lists) and report any core conflict.

Check the ring's example writes showcase/bestiarium/<slug>/: design.ring.json, report.json, finished-metal.stl, casting-pattern.stl (sand: mesh::try_build_pattern; wax: manufacturing::prepare), one reference-<stone>.stl per stone and stones.json (mesh, name, tint from Gem::preview_tint, ior, dispersion, roughness, transmission), and the hero/face/palm/side/shoulder/reverse/stones/bare-vs-finished renders. If stones.json is missing, add it to the example as Arachne's does.

Export and verify on current master: cargo build --offline --release -p ringdesign-core --example bestiarium_<slug>; systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G --quiet -- target/release/examples/bestiarium_<slug> showcase/bestiarium/<slug> --verify. Confirm every gate in report.json and diff it against the lane's committed report to say what the platform changed.

Add the ring to showcase/bestiarium/collection.json rings in sheet order: slug, title, subtitle (the epithet), description, spec (short, 'Process · stones', about 40 characters so the sheet stays legible), row (0 for sand, 1 for wax), centre, ortho_scale, exposed_controls ([] or names, {name, min, max} or bound entries {name, bind: [{kind|label, with, input}], min, max}), template_class. Recompute the collection subtitle (BEASTS · IN SAND · IN WAX · STONES), description and footer.

Template gate: cargo build --offline --release -p ringdesign-graph --example collection_templates; systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G --quiet -- target/release/examples/collection_templates bestiarium --only <slug> --verify-export. It writes graphs/templates/<slug>-bestiarium.graph.json and the ring's template.graph.json, editable-graph.ring.json and verification.json; require template_gate_passed, at most 4 design.set patches and the class budget.

Register: add TemplateGraph { name: <the design's name>, slug: "<slug>-bestiarium" } to BESTIARIUM in crates/ringdesign-graph/src/templates.rs in manifest order; add the slug to the Bestiarium group and to thumbnails! in crates/ringdesign-workbench/src/templates.rs; raise assert_eq!(slugs.len(), 53) by one.

Thumbnail: add "<slug>-bestiarium": {"source": "showcase/bestiarium/<slug>/hero.png", "size": [160, 160]} to crates/ringdesign-workbench/assets/templates/sources.json and run python3 tools/template_thumbnails.py <slug>-bestiarium.

Renders: systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=8G --quiet -- env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 blender -b --factory-startup -P tools/render_collection.py -- showcase/bestiarium <slug> --collection bestiarium (add --draft first to check centre and ortho_scale); then systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=4G --quiet -- python3 tools/catalog_collection.py showcase/bestiarium --collection bestiarium.
README: add the ring's table row, its verification column and bench notes, and its example to the reproduce commands.

Validate: cargo test -p ringdesign-graph --test bestiarium_templates and -p ringdesign-workbench --lib templates:: (paired unguarded build, guarded run), then every suite, the four-core CI emulation, all-targets with zero warnings, --locked, wasm and NDK.
Commit in steps: the merge; the refreshed outputs and manifest; the registration with the template and thumbnail; the renders, sheet, gallery and README.
